# CONTRIBUTING's good-first-issue link lists tickets someone already holds

## Context

On 2026-09-25 at 07:59Z, @amandeavor claimed #19143, 13 hours after it had been assigned to its first claimant. That claimant's PR, #19200, merged at 10:08Z, and the second claimant was redirected (issuecomment-5830488166). A first-time contributor's entry point is the good-first-issue link in `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 item 1. It lists every open labelled issue, assigned ones included, newest first. #19143 was the newest. We don't know whether this contributor arrived through that link, so the link is one cause among several.

## The Problem

An open, labelled issue reads as free. An assigned issue stays in the list until it closes, and the gap between assignment and close is where a second claimant lands. With Hacktoberfest opening on 2026-10-01, more claims will arrive while tickets are held.

## The Architectural Reality

- `CONTRIBUTING.md:115`: the good-first-issue link, `../../issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:117`: the help-wanted link, same shape. These two are the only such links outside `resources/content` (`git grep` on `dev`, 2026-09-25).
- GitHub search's `no:assignee` drops assigned issues. Measured at 10:14Z: good first issue 6 → 6 (the two held ones had just closed), help wanted 11 → 10.

## The Fix

Add `+no%3Aassignee` to both queries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Both links in `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 item 1 carry `no:assignee`. The PR body records each filtered query's count next to the unfiltered one at PR time.

## Out of Scope

- **`-linked:pr`.** It would also hide an issue that has an open PR but no assignee. #19062 was in that state while #19089 was open, because GitHub refuses to assign a user who never commented on the issue. But how GitHub treats a closed, unmerged PR's link is unverified, and a stale link would hide a free ticket permanently.
- **The claim responder.** Replying to second claimants is @neo-opus-grace's design under #18985.
- **More bug-shaped good first issues.** #19143 was the only bug among them, and both of today's claimants wanted a fix rather than a spec (@neo-opus-grace's reading). New ones are banked for 2026-10-01.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-25T10:23:45Z

Closing as not planned. The premise was wrong, as @tobiu pointed out. Contributors don't find good first issues through CONTRIBUTING's link. They find them through GitHub's own good-first-issue overviews, and those show whether an issue is assigned. #19143's second claim was made on the issue page itself, whose sidebar showed the assignee, so this filter wouldn't have changed anything. This body even named the arrival path as unknown; I measured the link's counts but never tested that premise. The pattern is handled where it happens: a fast reply to a second claim (#19202) and more bug-shaped good first issues, banked for 10-01. PR #19203 is closed unmerged. ⚖️ Ada
